kaps_punt: 'n voedselketting beskryf die voedsel verhoudings tussen plante en diere; 'n voedselketting begin met 'n plant (produseer kos), dan volg die dier wat die plant vreet, daarna 'n dier wat daardie dier eet, energie vloei van die plant deur tot by die laaste dier in die ketting

items.bewering: 'n Bees in die veld vreet die gras wat om hom groei.
items.bron: Noble Research Institute, 'Food requirements for different animals' (noble.org): cattle eat primarily grass; Wikipedia 'Cattle feeding'.

items.bewering: 'n Leeu vreet nie gras nie, maar hy vreet diere wat gras vreet.
items.bron: Lions are obligate carnivores and get no food from plant matter. They are sometimes seen chewing grass, but sources describe this as a non-food behaviour (probably to help digestion or make them vomit), not part of their diet (biologyinsights.com, 'Does a Lion Eat Grass?'; that source is weak, but the point that lions are carnivores is not in doubt). As a claim about what a lion eats as food, the sentence is correct. Springbok, which the lesson later gives as lion prey, do eat grass: they are mixed feeders (University of Pretoria, 'Feeding ecology of the Kalahari springbok', repository.up.ac.za/handle/2263/24111).

items.bewering: Elke dier se kos kom dus van 'n ander lewende ding af.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Food chain' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_chain): consumers feed on other organisms. Scavengers and animals that eat dead material eat things that were alive, so 'kom van 'n ander lewende ding af' still holds. Water and salt are not food in the sense used here.

items.bewering: 'n Voedselketting is 'n ry lewende dinge wat so aan mekaar vashaak. Dit wys wie wat vreet en in watter volgorde dit gebeur.
items.bron: Mapping check. A physical chain has links you could swap and no direction, but a food chain has a fixed direction. The lesson closes that gap itself in the next block ('Jy kan die skakels nie omruil nie, want elke dier vreet die een voor hom'), and it closes the 'a chain has a fixed end' gap with 'dan word die ketting langer'. Where a learner reasoning further would go wrong, the lesson has already said the opposite, so the mapping holds. Definition consistent with Wikipedia 'Food chain' (a linear sequence of who eats whom).

items.bewering: Elke voedselketting begin by 'n lewende ding wat sy eie kos maak.
items.bron: Ecology recognises two kinds of food chain. A grazing food chain begins with a producer, as the lesson says. A detritus food chain begins with dead material such as fallen leaves or dead animals, which decomposers and animals like earthworms eat. Source: NPTEL (IIT) Ecology course, Module 6 lecture 39 (archive.nptel.ac.in/content/storage2/courses/122103039/module6/lec39/2.html). Wikipedia 'Food chain' also says only that chains 'often' begin with an autotroph. Chains based on chemical energy (hydrothermal vents) still begin with something that makes its own food, so they are not a counterexample (NOAA Ocean Exploration chemosynthesis fact sheet). So 'Elke' is true for the kind of food chain CAPS describes and this lesson teaches, but it is not true of food chains in general. This is not something a writer can settle alone. The CAPS bullet itself says a food chain begins with a plant, and the lesson's 'voedselketting' entry defines the term the same way. A person needs to decide whether the universal stays, as CAPS's definition at Grade 5, or is narrowed. If it is narrowed, narrow the quantifier and not the subject, for example by referring to the chains in this lesson or to chains that begin in the veld or the sea. Because the energy in dead material also came from a producer, the lesson's energy story is unaffected either way.

items.bewering: Op die land is daardie lewende ding gewoonlik 'n plant.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Food chain': producers are autotrophs such as grass or algae. On land, primary production is overwhelmingly by plants (Field et al. 1998, Science, as summarised by the NASA Science Visualization Studio). 'gewoonlik' is properly qualified.

items.bewering: In die see is dit meestal alge.
items.bron: Flombaum et al. 2013, PNAS (via BioNumbers, bionumbers.hms.harvard.edu, id 112104): marine cyanobacteria (Prochlorococcus and Synechococcus), which are bacteria and not algae in Britannica's definition, make about 25% of ocean net primary production. Most of the rest comes from eukaryotic phytoplankton (algae such as diatoms) and seaweeds, so 'meestal' holds by share of food made. Caveats for a person: regional and review figures for cyanobacteria run much higher (30-80% in nutrient-poor tropical and subtropical waters; BioNumbers id 111683), and by NUMBER of cells, cyanobacteria outnumber algae. South African usage also calls cyanobacteria 'blougroen alge', which makes the sentence true in everyday Afrikaans as well. Not contradicted on the global picture.

items.bewering: Die meeste lewende dinge wat daar hulle eie kos maak, is te klein om met jou oë te sien.
items.bron: NASA (via scienceblog.com, quoting NASA's Michael Behrenfeld): phytoplankton are so small that hundreds side by side would be about the thickness of a coin; EurekAlert/NOAA image caption describes phytoplankton as single-celled. Most ocean producers by number and by share are microscopic phytoplankton.

items.bewering: Saam maak hulle omtrent die helfte van al die kos op Aarde.
items.bron: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio (svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/10497): phytoplankton are responsible for half of the photosynthesis on the planet; NASA technical report (ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20020090259): the ocean holds nearly half of Earth's photosynthesis; Field et al. 1998 (Science): land and ocean contribute about equally to global net primary production (ocean about 46%). 'omtrent die helfte' matches. Here 'hulle' refers to the microscopic producers in the sea, which is phytoplankton, so the antecedent is right whether or not cyanobacteria count as algae.

items.bewering: Die tweede skakel is die lewende ding wat die eerste skakel vreet. Die derde skakel is die lewende ding wat die tweede skakel vreet.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Food chain': each level feeds on the one before it (producer, primary consumer, secondary consumer).

items.bewering: Gras groei in die veld, en 'n springbok vreet daarvan. 'n Leeu vang daardie springbok en vreet hom op.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Springbok' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springbok): 'lions, spotted hyenas, and African wild dogs are predators of adult springbok'; springbok prefer grasses such as Themeda triandra when available. University of Pretoria dissertation on Kalahari springbok in the Kgalagadi (repository.up.ac.za/handle/2263/24111): springbok are mixed feeders, eating both grass and browse. Note for a person, not a fault: in Kalahari studies lions mostly kill gemsbok and blue wildebeest, and springbok matter more to leopards and cheetahs (Mills 1984, Koedoe). The lesson does not say springbok are a lion's main prey, so the example chain is true. The framing sentence 'Hierdie volgorde is maklik om in die veld te sien' is teaching framing, not a factual claim.

items.bewering: Jy kan die skakels nie omruil nie, want elke dier vreet die een voor hom.
items.bron: Follows from the definition of a food chain as a directed sequence of who eats whom (Wikipedia 'Food chain'). Within the chain described, swapping two links would make a link eat the one after it, which contradicts the chain.

items.bewering: Sommige kettings het vier lewende dinge
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Food chain': there are usually no more than five trophic levels in a food chain, so chains of three and four are common.

items.bewering: Gras groei langs die water, en 'n sprinkaan vreet stukkies daarvan af.
items.bron: Environmental Entomology 43(5), 'Evidence for diet-driven habitat partitioning of Melanoplinae and Gomphocerinae' (bioone.org, doi 10.1603/EN13349): Gomphocerinae grasshoppers are primarily grass feeders; Journal of Biosciences (link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12038-013-9325-8): some grasshopper species feed only on grasses. Many grasshoppers eat grass; the lesson's 'n sprinkaan' does not claim all do.

items.bewering: 'n Padda spring uit die water en vang die sprinkaan.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Frog' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frog): adult frogs generally eat small invertebrates, especially insects, which they seize with a sticky tongue. Grasshoppers are named as frog prey in several general sources, which agree with each other but are of low quality.

items.bewering: 'n Slang kom later daar verby en vreet die padda op.
items.bron: Keogh, Branch & Shine 2000, Journal of the Herpetological Association of Africa (nisc.co.za abstract 36019): 97% of recorded prey of the herald snake (rooilipslang, Crotaphopeltis hotamboeia) in southern Africa were frogs and toads. Kruger National Park species page (krugerpark.co.za): feeds at night on amphibians.

items.bewering: Die slang is die laaste dier in hierdie ketting. 'n Ander dier kan die slang nog vang, maar dan word die ketting langer.
items.bron: 'laaste' is limited to 'hierdie ketting' and is therefore definitional, not a claim about a top predator. Snakes are eaten by other animals: Davies et al., Ornithological Observations (journals.uct.ac.za/index.php/BO/article/download/251/292/738) records snakes as a small but real part of the secretarybird's diet, and SANBI's secretarybird page (sanbi.org/animal-of-the-week/secretarybird) lists its prey. Correct, and correctly qualified.

items.bewering: Eerste skakel: die gras langs die dam. / Tweede skakel: die sprinkaan wat die gras vreet. / Derde skakel: die padda wat die sprinkaan vang. / Vierde skakel: die slang wat die padda vreet.
items.blok: Die vier skakels by die dam
items.bron: Matches the chain in the block before it item for item; each feeding link is verified above (grasshopper sources Environmental Entomology 43(5); frog Wikipedia 'Frog'; herald snake Keogh, Branch & Shine 2000). The order is consistent with the study text.

items.bewering: Elke dier kry energie uit sy kos en gebruik dit om te lewe. Sonder energie kan 'n springbok nie hardloop of asemhaal nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Ecological efficiency' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecological_efficiency): energy taken in as food is broken down in respiration to run the body. Running and breathing are both muscle work, and EIA Energy Explained (eia.gov/energyexplained) describes motion as requiring energy.

items.bewering: Daardie energie kom byna altyd van die son se lig af.
items.bron: NOAA Ocean Exploration chemosynthesis fact sheet (oceanexplorer.noaa.gov/edu/materials/chemosynthesis-fact-sheet.pdf): food webs at hydrothermal vents and cold seeps run on chemical energy, not sunlight; Wikipedia 'Food chain': most life depends on sunlight through photosynthesis. 'byna altyd' is exactly the right qualifier.

items.bewering: Plante en alge vang daardie lig en maak daarmee hulle eie kos.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Algae' (britannica.com/science/algae): algae are photosynthetic organisms; Wikipedia 'Food chain': producers (grass, algae) make food using the sun's energy. The sentence does not say that ONLY plants and algae do this, so it does not contradict the cyanobacteria point above.

items.bewering: Die son is self nie 'n skakel nie, want 'n skakel is 'n lewende ding.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Food chain': a chain begins with an autotroph (producer), so trophic levels are organisms and the sun is the energy input, not a level. Some school diagrams draw the sun as the first box, but they label it as the energy source and not as a producer. The lesson's position matches ecological usage and its own 'skakel' definition.

items.bewering: By die dam loop die energie van die gras na die diere. Die gras hou daardie energie in sy eie kos vas. Die sprinkaan vreet die gras en kry 'n deel daarvan. Die padda vreet die sprinkaan en kry weer 'n deel daarvan. So loop die energie tot by die slang, die laaste dier in hierdie ketting.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Food chain': only part of the energy at one level passes to the next (about 10%), because the rest is used in metabolism. Producers store the captured energy in the food they make. The flow metaphor ('loop') maps correctly: the flow goes one way only, and the amount gets smaller at each step, which the lesson says. Nothing in it suggests energy comes back or grows.

items.bewering: Elke dier gebruik 'n deel daarvan om te lewe. 'n Deel van sy kos verlaat sy lyf onverteer. Daar bly dus minder oor vir die volgende dier.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Ecological efficiency': energy is lost between levels through respiration and through incomplete digestion, plus parts and organisms that are never eaten. The lesson names two real routes and does not claim they are the only ones, so the conclusion 'minder oor' is sound.

items.bewering: voedselketting: 'n Ry lewende dinge wat begin by een wat sy eie kos maak. Elkeen daarna vreet die een voor hom.
items.bron: This is the same question as the item on 'Elke voedselketting begin by 'n lewende ding wat sy eie kos maak' in 'Die volgorde van die skakels'. The definition describes a grazing food chain, which matches the CAPS bullet's wording, but detritus food chains begin with dead material (NPTEL (IIT) Ecology course, Module 6 lecture 39). The rest of the definition, 'Elkeen daarna vreet die een voor hom', is correct (Wikipedia 'Food chain'). A person decides whether the CAPS-level definition stands. If 'voedselketting' is a shared term for the subject-grade, any change has to be made to the shared definition and not in this lesson alone.

items.bewering: skakel: Een lewende ding op sy eie plek in 'n voedselketting.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Food chain': a chain is a linear sequence of organisms, each occupying a level. Accurate at this grade; a link stands for a kind of organism, and the lesson's examples (gras, sprinkaan, padda, slang) use it that way.

items.bewering: alge: Lewende dinge wat meestal in water groei en hulle eie kos maak. Hulle het nie regte wortels, stingels of blare nie.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Algae' (britannica.com/science/algae): algae lack true roots, stems and leaves; Britannica Kids: a group of predominantly aquatic photosynthetic organisms. 'meestal in water' is properly qualified (some grow on soil, bark or snow).

items.bewering: energie: Wat nodig is om iets te laat gebeur, beweeg of werk.
items.bron: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Energy Explained, 'What is energy?' (eia.gov/energyexplained): energy is the ability to do work and takes forms such as motion, heat and light. The lesson's wording is an accurate simplification of that standard definition.

opsomming: Nothing in the lesson is false, but a person must decide one curriculum-scope question that appears in two places: 'Elke voedselketting begin by 'n lewende ding wat sy eie kos maak', and the 'voedselketting' definition. Both are true of the grazing food chain CAPS describes, but ecology also recognises detritus food chains that begin with dead material, so the person either keeps the universal as CAPS's Grade 5 definition (accepting both items by name) or narrows the quantifier, in the shared definition if the term is shared.
